trigger: With legacyCloud=true, a CREATE collection is issued and its core CREATE to the target node is delayed in flight; meanwhile an operator unsets legacyCloud via CLUSTERPROP, and the delayed core CREATE (built in legacy mode, without coreNodeName) then reaches a node that now sees non-legacy mode.
reason: The triggers (a network delay and a concurrent CLUSTERPROP) are allowed, but the outcome is a correct rejection plus clean rollback. CreateCollectionCmd reads the mode once (CreateCollectionCmd.java:170) and in legacy mode does not pre-register replicas in state.json. In non-legacy mode a core without a coreNodeName has no state.json entry and cannot be registered, so CoreContainer.create rejects it (CoreContainer.java:1327-1330). That is the check doing its job of keeping legacy-style self-registration out of a non-legacy cluster. The Overseer then cleans up the half-created collection and reports failure (CreateCollectionCmd.java:394-396). The CREATE fails once, during an operator-initiated switch of a cluster-wide (deprecated) mode, with no lasting damage, and succeeds when retried.
